ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for banking AML risk tier 'Medium_Risk_Enhanced'. Screening must cover OFAC SDN/Blocked Persons, U.S. Denied Parties List, UN Consolidated Sanctions List, Colombian national lists (UIAF / Decreto 1736 de 2015), EU consolidated sanctions list and Interpol notices. All UBOs, directors, officers, attorneys-in-fact and material counterparties must be identified and risk-rated. PEP status of any shareholder, director, UBO or representative requires escalated approval and enhanced monitoring. Adverse media and sanctions search must be completed prior to incorporation, documented in writing, retained for no less than five (5) years, and be available to the Chamber, DIAN and UIAF upon inspection.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) - www.rues.org.co (operated by the Cámaras de Comercio network / Confecámaras)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Registered company names must be expressed in Spanish and in the Latin alphabet. Non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, etc.) must be transliterated to a phonetically acceptable Spanish rendering. Foreign words and acronyms are accepted only when clearly pronounceable in Spanish and sufficiently distinctive. All public filings, registrations and the certificate of incorporation must be in Spanish or accompanied by an official and sworn Spanish translation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Tokens of national government institutions such as 'NACIONAL', 'PRESIDENCIA', 'MINISTERIO', 'MUNICIPAL', 'DEPARTAMENTAL' unless prior authorization is obtained from the relevant ministry
Financial-sector reserved tokens requiring Superintendencia Financiera license: 'BANCO', 'SEGUROS', 'FIDUCIARIA', 'FONDO DE PENSIONES'
Professionally reserved terms: 'ABOGADO', 'MEDICO', 'CONTADOR', 'INGENIERO', unless the related collegiate license is held
Terms or combinations identical or confusingly similar to existing registered company names or trademark-protected names (homonimia rules)
Names implying international organizations or state entities, e.g., 'ONU', 'CRUZ ROJA', 'EMBAJADA'
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If RUES rejects a proposed company name, the applicant or its counsel may file a 'recurso de reposición' before the same Cámara de Comercio within ten (10) business days of notification. If denied, a 'recurso de apelación' may be filed within ten (10) business days before the Superintendencia de Sociedades. The appeal must state the exact RUES transaction ID, the proposed name, the rejection reasons and the legal/administrative arguments. The pending appeal preserves the name reservation for up to 30 days or until the appellate decision, whichever is earlier. Once administrative remedies are exhausted, the applicant may challenge the refusal before the administrative courts (jurisdicción contencioso-administrativa). As a faster alternative, the applicant may simply file a new name reservation through RUES without prejudice to the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a pure spot-brokerage wholesale company with no physical stock, provided the virtual-office provider maintains a permanent physical suite in the chose municipality, is staffed during normal business hours, accepts service of process and official correspondence, and permits third-party visits when requested by DIAN or the Cámara de Comercio. The virtual-office address must appear as the registered domicile on the RUT and the certificate of incorporation. A virtual office is not acceptable if DIAN or the Chamber determines the company lacks real commercial or administrative substance, or if the company later stores or inspects goods at that address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 20-25% in the first calendar year for a foreign-owned, medium-risk semiconductor-trading S.A.S. The probability increases to 35-50% if enhanced UBO/AML flags arise, if there is an unresolved name-reservation appeal, or if DIAN detects inconsistencies in RUT, ICA, or UBO filings. Unannounced inspections are carried out by DIAN and the local Chamber as part of the 'verificación de realidad' process, particularly for entities classified at enhanced AML risk.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Colombian Code of Commerce (Código de Comercio), Articles 19-52, 86-150; Law 1258 of 2008 (Ley 1258 de 2008), Articles 1-44; Decree 1074 of 2015 (Decreto Único Reglamentario del Sector Comercio), Articles 2.1.1.1.1 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Bogotá Chamber of Commerce (Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) acting through the Unique Business and Social Registry (Registro Único Empresarial y Social — RUES)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Private Incorporation Instrument (Documento Privado de Constitución) with accompanying RUES Single Registration Form (Formulario Único de Registro Empresarial y Social)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital under Law 1258 of 2008; the S.A.S. may be incorporated with a symbolic paid-in capital of one (1) share as long as subscribed capital does not exceed authorized capital and the paid-in term does not exceed two years. Capital may be contributed in cash, foreign currency, or in-kind hardware inventory; no escrow or bank-lock account is required by law, but paid-in capital in foreign currency must be reported under Banco de la República exchange circular regulations when remitted from abroad.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] S.A.S. On this [__] day of [______], 20__, the founding shareholders of [COMPANY NAME] S.A.S., acting under Law 1258 of 2008, the Colombian Code of Commerce, and the Company bylaws, resolve: 1. Share Subscription: Authorized capital of [COP] divided into [___] ordinary shares is hereby fully subscribed and paid; share certificates are issued. 2. Registered Office: Principal corporate domicile is adopted at [registered address], Bogotá D.C., Colombia. 3. Officers: [Name] is appointed General Manager and Legal Representative with broadest faculties, and [Name] is appointed Compliance Officer. Each motion passes unanimously; the corporate ledger and statutory books are opened.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá — RUES online homonym search portal (www.rues.org.co)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed corporate name to the RUES homonymy consultation module (homonimia). Declare ISIC 4651 (wholesale of computers, computer peripheral equipment, solid-state drives, and server processors) as the principal activity. If the search returns no identical or confusingly similar registered enterprise, request the homonymy certificate, which reserves the name for 30 calendar days.
required_dossiers: Completed RUES homonymy application form
Proposed corporate name (three alternatives recommended)
Digital copy of each shareholder's citizenship card or passport
Short description of the ISIC 4651 wholesale activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a homonym dispute is detected, file a written clarification with the Chamber President reasserting the distinguishing elements of the trade name; alternatively, submit three revised alternative names for a fresh RUES search at no additional charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution, Notarization, and Non-Resident Authentication of the Incorporation Instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of Bogotá D.C. (mandatory only if real estate is contributed; otherwise private document with option of authenticated signatures)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Documento Privado de Constitución containing the S.A.S. bylaws: corporate purpose limited to open-market brokerage of SSDs and server processors (ISIC 4651), authorized/subscribed/paid capital, domicile at the Bogotá registered address, term of duration, and legal-representation rules. When a shareholder is a foreign non-resident, their signature and corporate authorization must be legalized with an Apostille and submitted to the notary in certified translation; the same instrument must be fully executed before opening any bank account.
required_dossiers: Signed private incorporation instrument and full bylaws
Identity documents (passport or cédula) of all founding shareholders
Apostilled corporate resolution and power of attorney for non-resident shareholders
Bank certificate or notarized capital payment receipt when capital is contributed in cash
Accredited appraiser report for any in-kind hardware inventory contributed as capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or legal counsel lodges a defect in the instrument, execute a supplementary corrective deed (otorgamiento complementario) or amend the capital clause subject to shareholder approval and re-authenticate signatures within ten business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation and Commercial Enrollment with the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá — Company Creation Window (Ventanilla de Constitución de Empresas)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed incorporation instrument and the RUES registration form to the Chamber's virtual filing desk. Pay the single registration fee (derecho de registro and matrícula mercantil), then obtain (i) the Matrícula Mercantil certificate, (ii) the Pre-RUT voucher, and (iii) the certified seals (sello) for the official corporate books — shareholders' register, minutes book, and accountant's ledger (libros 606, 608, 607).
required_dossiers: Signed Documento Privado de Constitución
RUES single registration form
Valid homonymy certificate
Payment receipt evidencing the registration fee
Notarial authentication certificate when applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: When the Chamber returns an observation (observación), cure the referenced drafting defect within 30 calendar days and resubmit the corrected instrument without an additional filing fee; failing that, restart with a duplicate incorporation filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration (NIT-RUT) and Electronic Invoicing Activation with DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) — Central Office for Corporate Taxpayers and Virtual RUT Portal (muisca.dian.gov.co)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convert the Pre-RUT obtained from the Chamber into the definitive RUT through DIAN's virtual web portal; verify the issued NIT certificate and ensure the RUT reflects principal activity ISIC 4651 and the ICA (industry and commerce) tax registration attached to Bogotá D.C. Request authorization under the electronic invoicing system (facturación electrónica, Resolution 165 of 2023) and configure the TIN for inbound Swift TT wire transfers; register the legal representative's digital signature certificate issued by an ONAC-authorized certification authority.
required_dossiers: Pre-RUT voucher from the Chamber
Commercial enrollment certificate (Matrícula Mercantil)
Shareholders' and legal representative's identity documents
Lease or ownership contract of the registered office
Documentation of bank account and Swift TT receiving currency code
Declaration of beneficial owners and ultimate shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUT is blocked due to discrepancies, file an electronic 'solicitud de actualización, corrección o saneamiento del RUT' and attach the incorporation instrument plus Chamber certificate; escalate to the fiscal superior for delays exceeding five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Commerce Registration, Land-Use Permit, and Fire-Safety Clearance of Registered Premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Mayor's Office of Bogotá D.C. — Secretaría Distrital de Gobierno, Local Mayor (Alcaldía Local) and the Bogotá Fire Department (Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos de Bogotá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the physical premises in the municipal Registro de Industria y Comercio (RIyC) and request the certificate of compatible land use (uso de suelo) for wholesale warehousing of electronic components. Arrange for the fire department inspection of the office and storage room, providing maintenance certificates for portable extinguishers, emergency lighting, and posted evacuation signage; obtain the Matrícula de Industria y Comercio certificate, the Certificado de Bomberos, and, where the warehouse stores lithium-battery-containing devices, a battery-storage segregation approval.
required_dossiers: Municipal commerce registration request
Land use certificate application coordinated with the Local Mayor
Lease deed or property title for the Bogotá registered address
Fire extinguisher maintenance invoice dated within 60 days
Emergency plan and evacuation signage log for the warehouse
Inventory list declaring SSD/CPU stock and battery-containing electronic goods
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspection returns a list of nonconformities, install the specified extinguishers, signage, emergency exits, and battery containment racking, then request re-inspection within 15 business days; land-use denials may be appealed through the Secretaría Distrital de Gobierno's administrative review procedure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Secretaría Distrital de Desarrollo Económico de Bogotá (Bogotá District Economic Development Department) acting with the Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá for the municipal industrial and commercial registry
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro de Industria y Comercio (RIyC) — Municipal Operating License for Wholesale Trading and Matrícula Mercantil (Commercial Enrollment) for the physical establishment

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) with local execution by Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente (SDA) of Bogotá D.C.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category IV — Exempt from Full EIA: wholesale commodity brokerage of SSDs and server processors (ISIC 4651) is not listed under Decree 1076 of 2015 Title IV as an activity requiring a prior environmental license; however, the entity must register in the SDA waste-generator registry if the warehouse reprocesses, reworks, or stores returned defective electronics and must comply with Resolution 1672 of 2013 on extended producer responsibility for WEEE e-waste.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater is generated; office/warehouse sanitary discharges are governed by municipal sewer regulations and Resolution 0631 of 2015 general thresholds (pH 6.0-9.0, suspended solids ≤ 80 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 70 mg/L). VOCs must remain at trace levels; the warehouse must maintain a battery-safe segregation area with retardant racks for lithium-containing SSD/CPU stock and deliver all damaged electronics under an approved e-waste collection flow, reporting volumes to SDA in the single annual hazardous-waste declaration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Certificado de Bomberos issued by the Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos de Bogotá evidencing fire-safety compliance; structural load inspection certificate from the Curaduría Urbana where warehouse racking exceeds 500 kg/m²; employer registration with the occupational risk administrator (ARL) and an active programa de salud ocupacional for the stocking, packing, and inspection of electronics; plus the District Civil Defense risk-communication clearance for the storage site.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direccion de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); official portal: www.dian.gov.co; digital taxpayer platform: MUISCA / Sede Electronica DIAN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Colombian S.A.S. obtains its statutory tax identification and registration as follows: (1) Incorporate the Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada by private document or public deed and register it with the local Camara de Comercio in the company's registered office; minimum capital is not statutorily required and non-resident ownership is permitted. (2) After commercial registration, DIAN recognizes the company's NIT (Numero de Identificacion Tributaria) and creates its RUT (Registro Unico Tributario) record; the legal representative must file/update the RUT online through DIAN declaring the ISIC 4651 wholesale trade activity in respect of solid-state drives and server processors, and the applicable tax obligations (corporate income tax, VAT, and export-related registrations). (3) The S.A.S. must activate electronic invoicing credentials in DIAN's digital platform, obtain an authorized digital certificate for the legal representative or authorized users, and obtain the CUFE/CUDE stamping mechanism for export invoices. (4) A non-resident shareholder is not separately required to obtain a Colombian NIT merely by owning an S.A.S.; if the foreign entity itself establishes a permanent establishment or conducts independent Colombian-source taxable activity, it must appoint a Colombian tax representative and register through the RUT in its own name. (5) The RUT is a standing registration instrument and must be updated within the statutory periods upon changes in legal form, address, directors, shareholding, activities, or tax status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - a Colombian S.A.S. is a resident juridical person taxed at entity level on worldwide income; partnership or pass-through treatment is not available. A branch or permanent establishment of a foreign entity is also taxed at entity level on Colombian-source income. A non-resident without permanent establishment is generally subject only to Colombian-source withholding taxes, not to an entity-level return through a locally incorporated S.A.S.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombian tax law does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election or hybrid entity election for an S.A.S.; the S.A.S. remains a classic taxable corporation. Available elections and special regimes relevant to this profile include: (a) the elective 'Regimen Simple de Tributacion' (SIMPLE) for qualifying smaller entities with gross turnover not exceeding 3,500 UVT, which replaces the ordinary income-tax computation but does not make the entity pass-through; (b) voluntary registration as 'exportador' or customs-authorized user for streamlined export clearances; (c) election to operate as a Zona Franca user for goods physically admitted to a free-trade zone, which can affect VAT suspension and CIT rate; (d) election of special holding-company (CHC) treatment for dividends coming from foreign subsidiaries, subject to substance conditions; and (e) no unilateral hybrid-mismatch election, but Colombian CFC and transparency rules may cause foreign income to be attributed to Colombian shareholders. All elections are exercised through DIAN or the relevant customs authority and do not alter the S.A.S.'s fundamental entity-level tax character.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre las Ventas) - Colombian Value Added Tax, administered by DIAN and integrated with customs clearance controls.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary VAT registration turnover threshold applies to legal persons: an S.A.S. engaged in taxable sales is required to register in the RUT and to charge VAT from its first taxable transaction. The optional SIMPLE tax regime uses an annual 3,500 UVT gross-revenue ceiling for eligibility, but that ceiling is not the VAT registration threshold. VAT registration is event-based and is required regardless of turnover for the sale of goods and the provision of taxable services in Colombia.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing is mandatory for all VAT-responsible taxpayers. The S.A.S. must issue 'facturas electronicas de venta' through a DIAN-certified software or the DIAN public system, include the assigned CUFE (Codigo Unico de Facturacion Electronica) or CUDE for contingency, transmit each invoice for DIAN validation before delivery to the buyer, and include a machine-readable QR code. For export operations, the electronic export invoice and supporting transport/customs documents are transmitted to DIAN through MUISCA and the customs single window before the export declaration is definitively accepted; DIAN validates export-exemption claims and the exporter must retain the accepted clearance records and aggregated VAT refund schedules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Colombian VAT law provides an exempt-export treatment with economic effect equivalent to zero-rating for goods and certain offshore services, with refund of related input VAT. To claim the benefit for SSD and CPU chip wholesale exports, the exporter must establish: (1) the S.A.S. is registered in the RUT and has declared the export activity; (2) the goods are physically sold to a foreign buyer and leave Colombian customs territory under a definitive export procedure; (3) the electronic export invoice describes the goods under ISIC 4651 consistent with the customs declaration; (4) title and risk have passed to the foreign consignee outside Colombia; (5) for services, the benefit must be rendered to a foreign customer and used exclusively outside Colombia; and (6) the foreign currency proceeds are collected and repatriated through the Colombian foreign exchange market by the exporter. The exporter must maintain a complete documentary file for at least the statutory limitation period, ordinarily five taxable years.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaracion de Exportacion - DEX) accepted as definitive by DIAN customs authorities
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure of the SSD and CPU chips from Colombian customs territory
Commercial invoice and packing list consistent with ISIC 4651 wholesale trade and with the electronic export invoice
Electronic export invoice bearing the CUFE code and DIAN validation
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Reintegro de Divisas) issued by a Colombian authorized intermediary proving collection and repatriation of the export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN cross-checks export declarations, electronic invoices, transport documents, and foreign currency repatriation records. If an export zero-rating claim is found to lack a real exit, to be supported by false documents, to be linked to unrepatriated proceeds, or to involve a sham foreign transaction, DIAN will disallow and claw back the VAT refund (saldo a favor) and assess moratory interest from the date of the erroneous refund. The taxpayer may also be subjected to the statutory inaccuracy penalty, currently up to 160% of the tax understatement, and to penalties for incorrect electronic invoicing and for non-compliance with customs formalities. In flagrant cases involving false customs declarations or fraudulent refund schemes, the conduct may be reclassified as tax fraud or customs smuggling, attracting monetary fines, disqualification from export programs, and criminal liability. DIAN retains audit and assessment powers for the general five-year limitation period, extended further in cases of non-filing or omissions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (the Central Bank of Colombia), acting through its Junta Directiva, is the monetary and foreign-exchange authority. The governing instrument is the 'Régimen de Cambios Internacionales' contained in Resolución Externa No. 8 de 2000 (as amended), supplemented operationally by Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83 issued by Banco de la República. The Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) supervises the authorized foreign-exchange intermediaries ('intermediarios del mercado cambiario' or CAMs, i.e., Colombian commercial banks and licensed financial corporations); the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) administers export and import declarations and customs documentation; and the Unidad de Información y Análisis Financiero (UIAF) is the AML/CFT financial-intelligence unit. All cross-border trade settlements above the legal de minimis threshold must be channelled exclusively through CAMs; offshore digital payment providers are not authorized intermediaries under Colombian exchange law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) is floating and fully convertible on both current-account and capital-account transactions, subject to administrative channeling rather than to quantitative limits, prior-exchange licenses, or multiple-currency practices. Current-account operations (imports of goods and services, royalties, freight, commissions) may be executed freely through a CAM; operations whose value exceeds the US$50,000 per-transaction de minimis threshold must be settled via CAM and declared on the appropriate Declaración de Cambio (e.g., Formulario No. 5 for imports of goods), while operations at or below US$50,000 do not require channeling but remain subject to DIAN filing. Capital inflows (foreign direct investment, FDI) require no prior authorization: the non-resident shareholder may contribute capital to a Colombian S.A.S. through a CAM using Formulario No. 7 (Declaración de Cambio por Inversiones Internacionales), and the investment must be registered in Banco de la República's Registro de Inversiones Internacionales (RII) within six (6) months of the channeling date; registration is a statutory precondition for any subsequent dividend remittance, capital reduction, or repatriation of invested capital. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders face no FX quota, waiting period, or Central Bank approval once (i) the inward investment has been duly registered with the RII, (ii) Colombian corporate income tax and dividend-withholding taxes have been settled, and (iii) the remittance is executed through a CAM and reported on Formulario No. 7. There are no surrender requirements, no exchange-rate bands, and no forced conversion mechanisms for current-account proceeds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Colombia does not impose a mandatory surrender ratio or forced conversion of export receipts into COP; the operative statutory duty is 'canalización' through the authorized exchange market. The exporter must cause the foreign-exchange proceeds of goods exports to be paid into a CAM (either by selling the currency to the CAM at the market reference rate, the TRM, or by depositing it into a resident foreign-currency account maintained at a Colombian bank) within six (6) months counted from the date of the DIAN export declaration (Declaración de Exportación); this term may be extended by up to six (6) additional months (12-month cap) where justified causes are documented and accepted by the competent authority or the CAM under the applicable regime. Collections must be reported on Formulario No. 1 (Declaración de Cambio por Exportación de Bienes), distinguishing advance collections, on-arrival collections, and deferred collections, with the corresponding exchange finality codes (e.g., 81, 82, and 83). Export operations with an FOB value equal to or below US$50,000 are exempt from the mandatory channeling duty while remaining subject to DIAN export-filing requirements. Failure to channel within the prescribed term triggers administrative penalties by the SFC and/or DIAN under the exchange regime and may generate adverse tax presumptions regarding unrepatriated income.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational current account (COP) + resident foreign-currency account (USD) + fiduciary escrow and trade-finance facilities (Fiduciaria Bancolombia)
Operational current account (COP) + USD account + irrevocable documentary-credit issuance, open-account trade desk, and escrow/collection services
Operational current account (COP) + USD account + import letters-of-credit and foreign-trade clearing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Meeting approval of financial statements and legal reserve appropriation (Acta de Asamblea de Accionistas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company minute book (duly registered at the Chamber of Commerce upon filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months following the fiscal year-end (by March 31 for a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct chamber fine; non-approval prevents lawful dividend distribution and completion of annual statements registration; directors' liability for balance-sheet misstatements under Law 222/1995

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil (Mercantile Registry Renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of each year (renews the preceding calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly surcharge of 1% on renewal tariff plus fines of 1-17 UVT (approx. USD 12-210); after 1-2 years of non-renewal the chamber cancels the registration and the company loses legal standing to trade

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of audited annual financial statements with supporting notes (Estados Financieros de Fin de Ejercicio)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (register of books and corporate acts)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By April 30 (within one month after shareholder approval of the March 31 cut-off)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-registration fines of 1-17 UVT; refusal to issue certificado de existencia y representación, blocking credit, tenders and notarized acts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Regime update - Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Unidad Administrativa Especial Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the same NIT-based date set for the corporate income tax return (April-July); shareholding transfers must be reported within 30 calendar days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of 2,500 UVT (approx. USD 30,000) per Article 651-1 of the Tax Code; erroneous or omitted beneficial-owner data may trigger additional UBO-specific penalties and blocked RUT activities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Impuesto de Renta y Complementarios - Form 210)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between April and July, per the two-digit NIT calendar set for large and non-large taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine of 5% of income tax due (min. 10 UVT, max. 1,000 UVT); if no tax due, 0.5% of gross revenue up to 1,000 UVT; monthly default interest of approx. 1.2% on unpaid tax; DIAN may impose formal requirements with fines up to 160% of omitted tax

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit (Revisor Fiscal) mandatory when year-end total assets or gross ordinary income exceeds 5,000 SMMLV (COP 7,117,500,000 in 2025, approx. USD 1.7 million), or when the S.A.S. has more than 30 shareholders; below these thresholds the books must still be prepared and certified by a public accountant
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Colombia under Law 1314/2009: full IFRS for Grupo 1, IFRS for PYMES for Grupo 2; statutory statements prepared in COP with comparative prior-year figures

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: UBO declaration (RUB) must be restated annually by the date of the income tax return; the identification, country of residence and percentage of ownership of each direct and indirect beneficial owner must be current; a share transfer that changes beneficial ownership requires RUB update within 30 days and the transfer must be consistent with the shareholder ledger before dividend payments are made
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Libro de Registro de Accionistas (Register of Shareholders with transfer endorsements)
Libro de Actas de la Asamblea de Accionistas (Shareholders' Meeting Minute Book)
Libro de Junta Directiva (Board of Directors' Minute Book - if a board exists under the S.A.S. bylaws)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - 1,200 (annual legal representation and domicile support services in Colombia)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 8,000 (annual Revisor Fiscal / independent audit fee for a mid-size wholesale trader)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays or preferential corporate income tax rate apply to the wholesale trading of SSDs and CPU processors under ISIC 4651. The standard 35% rate applies. The only relevant incentive is the additional deduction of 50% for investments in science, technology, and innovation in certain cases, plus a reduced 25% rate for new entities established in designated ZES (Zonas Económicas y Sociales Especiales) if they meet employment and export thresholds; a wholesale broker without fixed Colombian operational substance will generally not qualify.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 210 – Declaración de Renta y Complementarios for Personas Jurídicas; filed electronically through the DIAN Muisca platform (www.dian.gov.co) using the authorized e-filing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual income tax return is due in accordance with the DIAN annual filing calendar, normally scheduled based on the last two digits of the NIT. For a calendar-year taxpayer (fiscal year ending 31 December), the deadline falls between early April and late June, i.e. within approximately 4 to 6 months after fiscal year-end. If a non-calendar fiscal year is used, the filing deadline is established by DIAN resolution relative to the specific year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: S.A.S. tax identification number (NIT) assigned by DIAN at incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Colombian entity reports its own NIT. Non-resident shareholders’ identification is not entered on this form; the entity’s NIT is sufficient.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All invoiced gross income from wholesale sales of SSDs, CPU chips, and semiconductor-related brokerage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include sales effectively generated by the Colombian S.A.S. regardless of whether the counterparty is abroad. Commissions retained by the S.A.S. for acting as open-market broker must be included in full as service income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 56 / Costos de ventas y costos de operación
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Purchases of semiconductor inventory, freight and logistics, customs duties, insurance, and directly attributable procurement costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where inventory is acquired from a related foreign supplier, the cost must be supported by a transfer pricing analysis; customs entries and the import declaration must substantiate the amount.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deductions, loss compensation, and adjustments. This is the base on which 35% income tax is computed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The S.A.S. computes this at entity level. Loss carryforwards are limited to 12 taxable years and cannot create a refund; they only reduce future taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount resulting from applying the 35% statutory rate to Box 84.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident shareholder is not taxed directly on this line. The entity must pay the assessed tax, and only dividends from after-tax profits may be distributed out of the S.A.S.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the assessed income tax for each month or fraction of month of delay, capped at 100% of the assessed tax; if there is no assessed tax, a fixed late-filing fine based on gross assets or taxable income applies. Default interest (intereses moratorios) accrues on unpaid tax from the original due date. Non-filing of the income tax return may trigger an official assessment by DIAN with an added penalty of up to 20% of the tax assessed plus interest.
